study type: secondary analysis of a multi-center randomized controlled trial
outcome: serious neonatal morbidities (NEC, PVL, IVH, BPD)
cohort: The study included 2,013 infants (226 preterm and 1,787 term) born to women with singleton pregnancies >=24 weeks gestation who underwent non-elective cesarean delivery.
finding: Exposure to adjunctive azithromycin antibiotic prophylaxis for non-elective cesarean delivery does not increase neonatal morbidity or mortality in term or preterm infants.
gest_age: >=24 weeks (stratified into preterm <37 weeks and term >=37 weeks, with mean gestational ages of 34 and 39.5 weeks respectively)
